title: Oddities: physically plausible rare outcomes that enter the chain as a cause at one input (GEN.1036)
status: the table and its vocabulary; rows are added by the modules that implement them (docs/design/systems/weird-worlds.md). Every rate is a rate on a gated population with its source, label, tier and tweak level, and a GEN.725 registry row.

body_type.label: kind of body
body_type.note: 't' for a terrestrial body, 'g' for a giant

eccentricity.label: orbital eccentricity
eccentricity.note: of the orbit about its star (a moon's: about its planet)

host_teff_k.label: star's effective temperature
host_teff_k.note: of the star the body goes round

host_mass_sun.label: star's mass
host_mass_sun.note: of the star the body goes round

host_close_binary.label: close binary host
host_close_binary.note: 1 when the body goes round a close pair, else 0

equilibrium_temperature_k.label: equilibrium temperature
equilibrium_temperature_k.note: from the light the body gets and its albedo

tidally_locked.label: tidally locked
tidally_locked.note: 1 when its day is its year, else 0

core_mass_fraction.label: core share of the mass
core_mass_fraction.note: iron core over the whole body

water_mass_fraction.label: water share of the mass
water_mass_fraction.note: all water, liquid, ice and bound

envelope_mass_fraction.label: gas envelope share of the mass
envelope_mass_fraction.note: hydrogen and helium over the whole body

collision_count.label: recorded giant impacts
collision_count.note: mergers the planet architecture recorded for this body

neighbour_period_ratio.label: closest neighbour's period ratio
neighbour_period_ratio.note: outer period over inner, 0 for no neighbour

forced_eccentricity.label: eccentricity forced by resonant neighbours
forced_eccentricity.note: from the planet's place in a resonant chain; left out for a planet in none

dayside_temperature_k.label: dayside rock temperature
dayside_temperature_k.note: the star's temperature times the square root of its radius over the orbit (no optical depth)

ring_from_fallen_moon.label: ring from a fallen moon
ring_from_fallen_moon.note: 1 when the planet's ring came from a moon the tide pulled inside the Roche limit, else 0

distance_over_host_radius.label: orbit in stellar radii
distance_over_host_radius.note: semi-major axis over the radius of the star the body goes round

rows.name: Iron-rich core

rate.source: registry row WR4: iron-rich rocky planets are 5 of 22 and 6 of 28 in Adibekyan and others 2021, about 1 in 21 in Plotnykov and others 2025 and none distinct in Brinkman and others 2024; log-uniform 0.01 to 0.23, middle 0.05
rate.label: READ

rows.source: [R2867]; Benz and others 2007 (Space Science Reviews 132, 189); Bonomo and others 2019 (Nature Astronomy 3, 416); the module is physics/mantle_stripping.py
rows.text: A giant impact knocked much of its rocky mantle off, so it is richer in iron than a planet that formed quietly, and its water went with it.

rows.name: Venus-type slow retrograde rotation

rate.source: registry row VS9: every moonless rocky planet with an air of 10 bar or more follows the closed-form tide balance of the module; the share that ends retrograde and slow is whatever share is born tilted past the split angle and old enough, which the census measures (no extra draw, and the design note's 25 percent is dropped)
rate.label: RECALLED

rows.source: [R0896] ([R0896]:767; 2003, Icarus 163:1 and 24); [R0962] (Int. J. Astrobiol. 14:233); the module is physics/venus_spin.py
rows.text: The star's heat tide on its thick air and the solid tide of the planet balance at a spin that is not the orbit's, so the planet turns slowly backwards, as Venus does.

rows.name: Extreme tilt seasons

rate.source: registry row SS20: the tilt is already drawn from the giant impacts that built the planet; the row names the tilts of 60 to 120 degrees (equal seasons for a tilt and its supplement) on a planet with no large moon, so there is no extra draw
rate.label: RECALLED

rows.source: [R2571] (Mars's chaotic tilt); [R2710] (Earth without the Moon); Uranus at 98 degrees; the module is physics/seasonal_swing.py
rows.text: Its axis lies far over, with no large moon to steady it, so the seasons are its main weather: each pole spends a season in daylight as bright as the equator's noon and a season in the dark.

rows.name: Resonant chain

rate.source: registry row WR8: 22 of 105 near-resonant first-order pairs librate (0.21), the pairs that keep a forced eccentricity; the chains themselves are found from the system's periods (module resonant_chains), so the gate already holds only a planet in a chain
rate.label: READ

rows.source: [R3220] Solar System Dynamics section 8.8; Lithwick, Xie and Wu 2012 (ApJ 761:122); TRAPPIST-1, Kepler-223, TOI-178 and Io, Europa and Ganymede; the module is physics/resonant_chains.py
rows.text: Its neighbours' pull keeps its orbit slightly eccentric, so its star's tide flexes it all the time, as Jupiter's moons flex Io.

rows.name: Highly eccentric orbit

rate.source: registry row RC6: the eccentricity is the generator's own draw (orbit_elements); the row only names the orbits at 0.5 or more, so there is no extra draw and the share is whatever the law gives, which the census compares with WR1
rate.label: READ

rows.source: HD 80606 b (e 0.93), HD 20782 b (e 0.95), Mercury, Pluto; [R4719]; the module is physics/orbit_oddities.py
rows.text: Its orbit is stretched so far that its year swings between a scorching close pass and a long, cold far one.

rows.name: Polar or retrograde orbit

rate.source: registry row WR2: 3 of 39 round cool hosts under 6,250 K; hot Jupiters (orbit under 10 stellar radii) with a stellar obliquity above 10 degrees at 3 sigma
rate.label: READ

rows.source: [R0061] (Winn and Fabrycky review) sections 3.1 and 3.7; [R0060]; Kepler-56, HAT-P-7 b; the module is physics/orbit_oddities.py
rows.text: Its orbit runs over the poles of its star, or against its spin, as many close giants round hot stars do.

rows.name: Disintegrating planet

rate.source: registry row DP6: every rocky planet that meets the module's gate (under 0.11 Earth mass, a period under a day, a dayside over 2,000 K) has the wind; the effect declines one the wind would already have used up; the design's 1 in 1,000 ultra-short-period planets (WR5, per star 0.0002 to 0.003) is what the census compares
rate.label: READ

rows.source: Kepler-1520 b, K2-22 b, KOI-2700 b; [R3487]; the module is physics/disintegrating_planet.py
rows.text: Its dayside is hot enough to lift a wind of its own rock vapor that its weak gravity cannot hold, so it is losing mass and trailing dust, and it will be gone.

rows.name: Ring from a fallen moon

rate.source: registry row RO19: the ring comes from the moon history already (GEN.1057), so there is no extra draw; the row names the rings whose origin is a moon the tide pulled inside the Roche limit
rate.label: READ

rows.source: Triton's decay, Phobos about 40 Myr from the Roche limit ([R1927] second-hand); the module is physics/moon_history.py (fallen_moons) and physics/ring_origin.py
rows.text: A moon spiralled in until the planet's tide tore it apart, and its pieces are the ring.

rows.name: Nightside collapse

rate.source: registry row NEB7: every rocky planet takes the model's answer, so there is no extra draw; the effect declines a planet that is not locked, has no air, or keeps half of its gas
rate.label: RECALLED

rows.source: [R4767] (Wordsworth and others, the critical pressure fit); [R2201]; the module is physics/nightside_collapse.py and docs/design/composition/nightside-collapse-model.md
rows.text: Its star's tide holds one face to the star for ever, and its thin air has frozen out onto the dark side, leaving the day side bare.

rows.name: Other climate branch

rate.source: registry row NEB8: no survey says which branch a world in the window ended in, so half of the worlds that hold two stable climates sit on the one the airless start does not find; the second solve is made only for a rolled world whose first answer is cool enough to be near the window (WR7 gives the window's width, 0.10 to 0.15 of the flux, which the solver finds for itself)
rate.label: RECALLED

rows.source: [R0580, R4008] (the ice-albedo feedback); WR7; the module is physics/climate_branches.py and physics/air_branches.py
rows.text: Its light is in the band where a world can be either warm or frozen over, and history put it on the other one.

rows.name: Giant tipped by an impact

rate.source: registry row GT4: the tilt is already drawn (giant_tilt.tilt_after_merger_deg, the merger share GT3 and the turn of one impact); the row names the giants of 5 to 30 Earth masses the draw left tipped 60 degrees or more, so there is no extra draw
rate.label: READ

rows.source: [R2300, R3149] (Uranus at 98 degrees by a giant impact); the module is physics/giant_tilt.py
rows.text: A giant impact knocked it over, and it turns on its side, its poles taking turns facing the star; its rings lie in the same tipped plane.
